title: Integer Fourier coefficients for polynomial thresholds
statement: Let $n$ and $d$ be nonnegative integers, and let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{\\pm1\\}$ be a Boolean function that has a polynomial threshold representation of Fourier degree at most $d$. Then there is a real-valued function $p$ on the cube such that $f(x)$ is the sign of $p(x)$ for every $x$, the Fourier degree of $p$ is at most $d$, every Fourier coefficient of $p$ is an integer, and $p(x)\\ne 0$ for every $x\\in\\{-1,1\\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube
$f$ has a polynomial threshold representation of Fourier degree at most $d$
